In [[complex analysis]] (a branch of [[mathematical analysis]]), the '''pseudo-zero set''' or '''root neighborhood''' of a [[degree of a polynomial|degree]]-''m'' polynomial ''p''(''z'') is the set of all [[complex number]]s that are roots of polynomials whose [[coefficient]]s differ from those of ''p'' by a small amount. Namely, given a [[norm (mathematics)|norm]] {{abs|·}} on the space <math>\mathbb{C}^{m+1}</math> of polynomial coefficients, the pseudo-zero set is the set of all zeros of all degree-''m'' polynomials ''q'' such that {{abs|'''''p''''' − '''''q'''''}} (as vectors of coefficients) is less than a given ''ε''.
